standard.title: Compare Perspectives and Explain Influences on Historical Perspective
standard.description: compare perspectives and explain how perspectives are influenced by significant events, ideas, location, beliefs and values
standard.prior_knowledge: In Year 7 students identified perspectives, attitudes and values in sources (AC9HH7S06). In Year 8 they continued with identification (AC9HH8S06). Y9 lifts the demand — from identify to compare, and adds the new requirement to explain how perspectives are influenced by events, ideas, location, beliefs and values. Students must now move from recognising different perspectives to explaining what shaped them.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students compare perspectives and explain how perspectives are influenced by significant events, ideas, location, beliefs and values.

nodes.label: Comparing perspectives across sources
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can determine whether information in one source can be verified by another and compare the range of perspectives surrounding a historical event.
nodes.minimum_width: Compare the perspectives in at least two sources about the same event, identifying at least one specific difference.
nodes.typical_width: Determine whether information in one source can be verified by another; compare and contrast the range of perspectives surrounding a historical event, including voices that may be absent from dominant sources (women, First Nations peoples, minority groups, colonised peoples); discuss whether an individual perspective is representative of a majority or minority view at the time.
wider: Compare perspectives from sources representing absent or marginalised voices (First Nations Australians, women, colonised peoples) alongside dominant-perspective sources — examining whose voices are systematically absent and why
Investigate one historical event using sources from three or more different national or social perspectives — practising the expansion of perspective beyond the binary

Examine how the same event is narrated in sources produced at three different times (contemporaneous, 50 years later, contemporary) — assessing how temporal distance influences perspective and what new perspectives emerge over time

response_modes.reason: Comparing perspectives across multiple sources — especially including absent voices — is the defining task here. Students who only compare two easily accessible perspectives (e.g. two Allied perspectives on WWI) are not meeting the full demand of the descriptor.

success_criteria: Compares the perspectives in at least two sources, identifying specific differences in what each presents
Identifies at least one voice or group whose perspective is absent or underrepresented in the available sources, and explains why

nodes.label: Explaining what influences perspective
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how a person's perspective is influenced by significant events, ideas, location, beliefs and values, demonstrating understanding of why people in the same period held different views.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain at least two factors (from: events, ideas, location, beliefs, values) that influenced the perspective shown in one source.
nodes.typical_width: Explain how perspectives are shaped by significant events, ideas, location, beliefs and values — connecting each source's perspective to the specific circumstances of its author; discuss whether an individual's perspective is representative of a majority or minority at the time; apply this across multiple sources and source types from the topics being studied.
wider: Apply perspective influence analysis to contrasting topic contexts — e.g. explaining what influenced a WWI soldier's perspective and what influenced a First Nations leader's perspective on colonisation — demonstrating the skill across different subject areas

Construct a structured comparison of two perspectives using an explicit framework: for each perspective, identify the events, ideas, location, beliefs and values that shaped it — then assess which factors were most influential

Examine how a person's perspective changed over time within their own lifetime (e.g. a politician's views on conscription before and after the referendum) — applying perspective analysis longitudinally

response_modes.reason: Applying perspective influence analysis across multiple contexts (different topics, different source types) develops genuine analytical transferability — the skill should work for WWI sources, colonial sources, and industrial era sources alike.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Explaining what influences perspective is a genuinely transferable historical thinking skill with application in all four depth studies. Practising it across multiple task contexts in the same year develops the skill to a level of genuine independence.
success_criteria: Explains at least two factors that influenced the perspective shown in one source, connecting each factor to specific evidence from the source
Explains how perspectives are shaped differently depending on the social position, beliefs, or experiences of the author
